evidence.summary: CASI describes the National University of Defense Technology in Changsha as a PLA university: founded in 1953 as the PLA Military Academy of Engineering in Harbin, it took its present name in 1978 and was rebuilt in 2017 with several other PLA schools, including the University of International Relations, the Xi’an Communication Institute and the College of Electronic Engineering. Its own publications say it carries out research on advanced weapons and equipment and key defence technologies, credit it with the Tianhe supercomputers, BeiDou satellite navigation work, hypersonic propulsion and laser gyroscopes, and count ten national-level and 12 military key laboratories.

Its admissions brochure describes it as directly under the Central Military Commission; CASI adds that it is most likely run through the commission’s Training and Administration Department and that its grade was lowered to corps leader in 2018.
